title: Choose core content by consensus
statement: Choose core content by how many independent sources include it, with a fixed inclusion threshold.
example: One social studies set drew on 16,345 standards from 51 jurisdictions and kept only content at its moderate threshold or above.
detail: A consensus social studies standards workbook records its method: consensus thresholds (CORE 38+, HIGH 26-37, MODERATE 13-25, LOW <13) over standards drawn from 51 jurisdictions, a resolution principle that favours knowledge-rich, recently revised standards where its backbone states conflict, and a note that a skills-only framework carries no content mandates (`downloads/5. Curriculum/Texts/Misconception and alignment checks/Social studies/Consensus social science standards.xlsx`, sheet 'Methodology Notes'). Its first tab includes only standards at MODERATE or above. It is a method; no outcome was measured. Settle conflicts in favour of the knowledge-rich, recently revised source, and do not rely on a skills-only framework alone.

evidence.quote: Skills only - no content mandates, no assessments
Weight powerful knowledge over popularity: 0.75 load / 0.25 frequency (the G3 dial, inherited deliberately).
"what the field commonly teaches" is a set of other people's design choices, not a discovered structure, so it carries *less* authority than powerful/portable knowledge.
Identity / Belonging / Friendship — REJECT, Load 3.0 / Weighted 4.03 (frequency 5/7, the highest).
